originalFailure.source: CLI complete-final5, worktree custom-parent postgres sibling case
originalFailure.cause: EPERM at first owner temporary-file rename. This occurs before its heartbeat starts; the original handle owner was not captured. Do not attribute the historical event to antivirus or this process's own heartbeat without evidence.

protocol: Exclusive lock directory -> complete primary/backup owner records -> worker heartbeat with token ownership probe -> records updated with probe port -> critical section -> verified release. Stale/heartbeat/acquisition intervals are retained.
changes: Windows rename retries only EPERM/EACCES/EBUSY, with a one-second retry window for the same complete prepared file; no target unlink, fallback payload, or port-assertion changes.

A lock-dir identity and owned file identity ledger span acquisition/publication/release. Temp creation is wx; every retry checks original non-reparse dir/temp and requires target absent for initial publication or matching the recorded target inode for rewrite.

Failure cleanup removes only observed matching entries and then an empty original directory, preserving unknown/replaced entries and replacement lock directories. Unexpected cleanup errors remain visible as AggregateError rather than being swallowed.
Only mkdir EEXIST means lock contention. A publication temporary-file collision cannot accidentally enter stale-lock recovery.
Windows process identity runs the fixed SystemRoot PowerShell executable with a ten-second deadline. A live PID with unavailable identity is retained, rather than being treated as proven PID reuse.
newWindowsCoverage: Real source-file handle omitting FILE_SHARE_DELETE causes actual rename EPERM/EBUSY; release is gated on the actual error. Both sync and async critical sections receive complete matching owner copies.
A permanently held handle exceeds the retry window and never enters the critical section.
Actual temporary inode replacement, actual lock-dir replacement and exclusive-temp collision preserve the competing bytes/paths and refuse entry.
Actual first/rewrite target replacement after a real sharing failure is observed and refused without overwriting the competing target.

Controlled native powershell.exe impersonator in both CWD and PATH is not run by the fixed-path implementation. Existing native CLI fixture bridge compiles fixed local no-network code into owned temporary paths.
A real live PID, closed probe and unavailable OS identity executable keep original owner bytes and lock inode unchanged until the existing acquisition deadline rejects.

limits: Identity checks are observations around path-based filesystem operations, not descriptor-atomic security against all same-directory TOCTOU interleavings.
Unknown/replaced entries are retained by immediate owned cleanup; existing stale-lock reclamation semantics outside this operation remain separate.
The original historical EPERM handle ownership is unknown. The controlled sharing-handle reproduction proves a real Windows failure class and the bounded recovery, not the historical reader identity.
The separate CLI observed ACL false has not been reproduced and its ten-second inspector deadline is unchanged; root-agent diagnostics are reported separately.
